{{nihongo|'''Izanagi Jingū'''|伊弉諾神宮}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} in the Taga neighborhood of the city of {{ill|Awaji, Hyōgo|en|Awaji, Hyōgo|qid=Q373107|lt=Awaji}} in {{ill|Hyōgo Prefecture|en|Hyōgo Prefecture|qid=Q130290|lt=Hyōgo Prefecture}}, {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|qid=Q17|lt=Japan}}. It is the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of former {{ill|Awaji Province|en|Awaji Province|qid=Q1053717|lt=Awaji Province}}. The main festival of the shrine is held annually on April 22. <ref>{{cite book |last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese}}</ref> 

==Enshrined ''kami''==
The ''[[kami]]'' enshrined at Izanagi Jingū are:
* {{nihongo|'''[[Izanagi|Izanagi-no-mikoto]]'''| 伊弉諾尊 |}}
* {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Izanami|en|Izanami|qid=Q682306|lt=Izanami-no-mikoto}}'''| 伊弉冉尊 |}}

==History==
Per [[Japanese mythology]] as outlined in the ''[[Kojiki]]'' and ''[[Nihon Shoki]]'', the [[Japanese archipelago]] (starting with {{ill|Awaji Island|ar|أواجي (جزيرة)|az|Avaci adası|bcl|Isla nin Awaji|be|Авадзі (востраў)|bg|Аваджи (остров)|bn|আয়াজি দ্বীপ|ca|Illa d'Awaji|ceb|Awaji Shima|cs|Awadži|da|Avaji|de|Awaji-shima|el|Αβάτζι|eo|Aŭaĝi|es|Isla Awaji|et|Awaji saar|eu|Awaji uhartea|fa|جزیره آواجی|fi|Awaji|fr|Awaji-shima|gl|Illa de Awaji|he|אוואג'י (אי)|hi|अवाजी द्वीप|hy|Ավաձի (կղզի)|id|Pulau Awaji|it|Isola Awaji|ja|淡路島|ko|아와지섬|la|Insula Awaji|lb|Awaji-shima|lt|Avadžis|nl|Awaji (eiland)|pl|Awaji (wyspa)|pt|Ilha Awaji|ro|Insula Awaji|ru|Авадзи (остров)|sl|Avadži (otok)|sv|Awaji|tg|Ҷазираи Авадзӣ|th|เกาะอาวาจิ|tr|Awaji Adası|uk|Авадзі|vi|Awaji (đảo)|wuu|淡路岛|zh|淡路島|qid=Q504373|lt=Awaji Island}}), the ''[[kami]]'', and all living things were created by the progenitor gods Izanagi and Izanami. After this work was completed, Izanagi retired into seclusion on Awaji Island where his tomb was located on the site of his palace. The documentary history, mention of a shrine to Izanagi in Awaji is made in an entry in the ''Nihon Shoki'' under the reigns of [[:en:Emperor Richu|Emperor Richu]] and {{ill|Emperor Ingyō|en|Emperor Ingyō|qid=Q349258|lt=Emperor Ingyō}} and the shrine appears in the ''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' in an entry dated 859.  In the 927 ''[[Engishiki]]'', it is listed a ''Myōjin Taisha'', and as the ''ichinomiya'' of the province. According to the records of nearby Myokyo-ji, Tamura Nakazane, a descendant of [[Sakanoue no Tamuramaro]], rebuilt the shrine in 1280. The Tamura clan served as hereditary ''[[kannushi]]'' and as local feudal lords into the {{ill|Sengoku period|en|Sengoku period|qid=Q204023|lt=Sengoku period}}. In 1581, {{ill|Oda Nobunaga|en|Oda Nobunaga|qid=Q171411|lt=Oda Nobunaga}} ordered Tamura Tsuneharu to take the lead in a battle against [[Takeda Katsuyori]], but he was defeated and the Tamura clan were destroyed. During the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period}}, the shrine was supported by the [[:en:Hachitsuka clan|Hachitsuka clan]], ''[[:en:Daimyō|Daimyō]]'' of {{ill|Tokushima Domain|en|Tokushima Domain|qid=Q3034557|lt=Tokushima Domain}}. During the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}} era of {{ill|State Shinto|bn|রাষ্ট্রীয় শিন্তৌ|de|Staats-Shintō|es|Sintoísmo estatal|fa|شینتوی حکومتی|fr|Shintoïsme d'État|id|Shinto Negara|ja|国家神道|ko|국가신토|no|Statsshinto|pt|Xintoísmo estatal|ru|Государственный синтоизм|simple|State Shinto|tr|Devlet Şintoizmi|vi|Thần đạo Quốc gia|zh|国家神道|qid=Q1197248|lt=State Shinto}}, the shrine was designated as a {{nihongo|National shrine, 2nd Rank |国幣中社|[[:en:Kokuhei Chūsha|Kokuhei Chūsha]]}} in 1871 under the [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto Shrines]]. It was promoted to an {{nihongo|Imperial shrine, 1st Rank |官幣大社|Kanpei Taisha}} in 1885. <ref>Ponsonby-Fane, Richard. (1959). ''The Imperial House of Japan,'' pp. 125.</ref>

In 1932, Izanami was added to the roster of the shrine, which in 1954 was renamed from Izanagi Jinja to Izanagi Jingū.<ref name="Okada">{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}}</ref>

The ''[[Honden]]'' is a three-bay ''[[Nagare-zukuri]]''-style building connected to the [[Heiden (Shinto)|Heiden]] by a roof. It was built on the site of the alleged tomb of Izanagi in 1882. The site had previously been a "forbidden land" upon which trespass was strictly forbidden for centuries. The Zuishin-mon on the approach to the shrine was completed in 1883.  The Kamiike pond in the precincts is said to be the remains of a moat which once surrounded the ruins of Izanagi's palace and tomb. <ref name="Yoshiki">{{cite book |last1=Yoshiki |first1=Emi |title=Zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' tettei gaido |date=2007 |publisher=PHP Institute |isbn=978-4569669304 |language=Japanese}}</ref>
